title: Mistral’s new Large 4 trails some Chinese open models in independent tests
key_facts: Mistral launched Large 4 (ML4), a trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters, in research public preview; weights are promised by the end of October.
Artificial Analysis (AA) scored it 38 on its Intelligence Index, the best from outside the US and China.
At least five Chinese open models scored higher: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 39, GLM-5.3-Flash 42, Kimi K3 44, GLM-5.3 45, MiMo-V2.6-Pro 46.
Cost per AA task is $1.13 at list price ($0.57 with a two-week 50% launch discount), against $0.25 for GLM-5.3-Flash and $0.13 for MiMo-V2.6-Pro.
Its strongest result is 81.7% on CyberGym-E2E-AA, but only 16% on DeepsecBench-AA and 51% on CWE-Bench-AA, the other two Cyber Index tests.
Mistral says it was trained on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European data centres.
AA lists the preview as proprietary until weights arrive and the model may be re-scored then.
quote_evidence: ML4 scored 38 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, which AA says makes it the "most intelligent model from outside the US and China."
At least five Chinese open models scored higher on the index: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max) at 39, GLM-5.3-Flash at 42, Kimi K3 (max) at 44, GLM-5.3 (max) at 45, and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 46.
Once it does, the model may be re-scored, and Mistral's claims will be held to task.
why_it_matters_hint: First independent ranking of Mistral's flagship puts Europe's best model behind several cheaper Chinese open models.
event_date: Launch about 6 Oct 2026; AA results and Tom's Hardware piece 9 Oct 2026
notes: Follow-up of the 7 Oct 2026 pool item (Reuters: Mistral launches AI model it says outperforms some Chinese rivals). Tom's Hardware quotes Reuters for CEO Arthur Mensch's remarks. Benchmark numbers are AA's; some performance claims are Mistral's.
